Our Mission

At Palo Alto Networks®, we’re united by a shared mission—to protect our digital way of life. We thrive at the intersection of innovation and impact, solving real-world problems with cutting-edge technology and bold thinking. Here, everyone has a voice, and every idea counts. If you’re ready to do the most meaningful work of your career alongside people who are just as passionate as you are, you’re in the right place.

Who We Are

In order to be the cybersecurity partner of choice, we must trailblaze the path and shape the future of our industry. This is something our employees work at each day and is defined by our values: Disruption, Collaboration, Execution, Integrity, and Inclusion. We weave AI into the fabric of everything we do and use it to augment the impact every individual can have. If you are passionate about solving real-world problems and ideating beside the best and the brightest, we invite you to join us!

We believe collaboration thrives in person. That’s why most of our teams work from the office full time, with flexibility when it’s needed. This model supports real-time problem-solving, stronger relationships, and the kind of precision that drives great outcomes.

Job Summary

Levels we are considering: Sr. Staff and Principal Engineers

Location: Santa Clara, CA (Hybrid: 3 days/week on-site at Corporate HQ)

Team: AIRS (Artificial Intelligence Runtime Security)

About the Team

Palo Alto Networks is pioneering the world’s most comprehensive AI security platform through Prisma AIRS—protecting complex ecosystems of AI models, applications, and agents from development through runtime.

We are building a brand-new initiative within the AIRS team focused on advancing state-of-the-art AI/ML infrastructure and high-performance, distributed backend systems. We are recruiting senior technical leaders to drive this architecture from the ground up.

The Role

As a senior technical leader on the AIRS team, you will operate at the intersection of machine learning, cloud security, and AI safety. You will design, build, and deploy high-performance infrastructure and autonomous ML solutions that actively classify threats, tune models, and prevent adversarial attacks at enterprise scale.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop scalable anomaly detection pipelines to monitor cloud environments and AI agent actions, ensuring high efficacy with low false-positive and false-negative rates.
• Lead SLM (Small Language Model) tuning initiatives, optimizing and fine-tuning models for low-latency, highly accurate edge-cloud security tasks.
• Drive advanced data classification strategies, applying machine learning, NLP, and deep learning methods to massive structured and unstructured datasets to extract complex threat patterns.
• Be a technical leader who partners closely with product, security, and cloud engineering teams to integrate these ML solutions seamlessly into production systems.

Qualifications

• Education & Experience: MS or PhD in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience) with 8+ years of software engineering industry experience, including a minimum of 3 years dedicated to machine learning, NLP, or AI systems.
• Programming & Frameworks: Deep programming expertise in Python and strong hands-on experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
• Large/Small Language Models: Proven experience working directly with LLMs/SLMs, advanced prompt engineering, and model fine-tuning techniques.
• Core ML Systems: Strong, demonstrated background in building and scaling auto-classification and anomaly detection models on massive, real-world datasets.

Additional Experience:

• Adversarial & Model Safety: Demonstrated knowledge of cybersecurity concepts and AI safety vulnerabilities (e.g., prompt injection defense, AI red-teaming, model security).
• Models & Frameworks: Familiarity with DistilBERT and other open-source classification models.
• Graph Architectures: Familiarity with large, graph-based datasets and processing techniques.
• Cloud Infrastructure: Experience with distributed cloud systems (GCP or AWS) and deploying scalable ML inference pipelines at scale.

We’re trailblazers that dream big, take risks, and challenge cybersecurity’s status quo. It’s simple: we can’t accomplish our mission without diverse teams innovating, together.

TL;DR

You're a communications professional who can plan and execute the work that advances Lovable's objectives across EU and Swedish policy environments, making sure our voice is heard on the issues that matter most. You'll pair sharp corporate communications with real policy fluency — working closely with internal teams and external partners to help policymakers, media, and other stakeholders understand Lovable's perspective on the key files and issues that shape the environment we operate in.

This is a balanced role, equal parts policy operator and corporate communicator. You'll report to the European Communications and Public Affairs Lead.

WHY LOVABLE?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

This role makes sure Lovable has a credible, constructive voice in the rooms that matter — building a presence worth listening to and developing clear positions that reflect what Lovable actually builds and believes.

Advocate Lovable's positions on key policy files. You'll build and run our engagement with policy representatives across EU and Swedish institutions.

Own corporate communications on policy issues. Statements, briefings, op-eds, speaking moments, and the proactive announcements that build credibility over time. You'll develop the strategy, write the materials, manage media relationships, and make sure each piece reinforces the others.

Track the regulatory agenda and turn it into a point of view. You'll monitor the files that affect us and develop clear positions that reflect the company's reality and ambitions.

Build coalitions and work through industry. You'll represent Lovable in trade associations and industry groups, finding shared causes that move issues forward.

Act as a comms and policy partner to our cross-functional team. You'll work closely with the communications and cross-functional teams in preparing for engagements with policymakers, institutions, and press, strengthening the company’s voice in the European AI debate.

WHO YOU ARE

You've operated in and around the policy world. That might mean an EU institution, a trade association, a think tank, or a public affairs firm. Wherever you've been, you know how a file moves from idea to law, and you can read the politics, formal and informal, that determine what actually happens.

You understand policy and can communicate it. You have experience from both policy work and corporate communications, and you're equally comfortable speaking to policymakers and media alike.

You can drive an issue forward in a complex political environment. You're comfortable with ambiguity and competing agendas, and you know how to prioritize when everything feels urgent.

You're a sharp writer with editorial judgment. You can turn a dense regulatory development into a crisp briefing, opinion piece or clean position statement.

You connect dots that other people don't see. You look at a piece of draft legislation and think ahead on what it means for the industry as well as what Lovable should say and to whom.

You're a genuine cross-functional collaborator. You work easily with cross-functional stakeholders, external partners, and coalitions. You don't wait to be invited into the room. You're not precious about who gets credit. You just make things work.

You're deeply curious about AI, technology policy, and the industry landscape. You keep up with what happens in the world instinctively — the news, the regulatory moves, the debates as they unfold. You understand where the conversation is heading well enough to spot a risk or an opportunity before someone hands it to you.

WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW

This is not a role where you set the strategy and hand off execution. You'll be writing the first drafts of our position statements, building the relationships and showing up in the room as a Lovable representative.

We move fast and plans change. The job runs on two clocks at once: you'll react to the urgent issue that lands today while building the relationships and positions that set us up for success in the long term. If you need a settled environment with predictable workflows, this will be frustrating. If you find that kind of pace energizing, you'll love it.

We're building public affairs and communications at a company that is itself being built. That means you'll have real influence over how this function develops in Europe: the positions, the relationships, the standards. That's the upside of being early.

Finally: joining Lovable Comms means you're deeply curious, data-driven, and not extremely precious about role boundaries. You find ways to work smarter with AI, to measure what matters, and to step into work that isn't technically "yours" when the moment calls for it.

ABOUT YOUR APPLICATION

Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.

We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

About the Team

Our sales and partner management teams are the heart and soul of DoorDash, enabling us to sign and partner with top restaurants across the country to drive revenue and help our partners operate and grow their businesses. As DoorDash grows both in scale and breadth of offering, the strength of our sales engine and organizational structure must grow with it.

About the Role

As the Manager of Sales Strategy & Operations for Sales Tooling, you will be the core DRI for DoorDash’s third-party (3P) technology ecosystem. You will play a pivotal role in executing against top company business objectives by owning the 3P portfolio of our centralized Sales tooling operation. Reporting to the Senior Manager of Sales Tooling, you will manage spend tracking and license optimization across the 3P budget, ensuring that every tool in our stack directly contributes to sales productivity and operational efficiency.

Strategic Ownership & Governance:

• Oversee the end-to-end strategy and execution of DoorDash’s 3P sales tooling portfolio.
• Act as a thought partner on “build vs. buy” decisions as it relates to our 3P vs 1P stack of sales tools.
• Operate and continuously improve the tooling governance process (intake, scoring, SLAs, and routing to Legal, Security, and Procurement) to eliminate redundant "shadow" procurement across lines of business.
• Run structured tool evaluations, make scale or sunset recommendations to the governance council, and execute approved procurement and decommissioning.

Cross-Functional Partnership:

• Gather and synthesize requirements from Sales teams to shape tool selection and feature asks.
• Partner with GTM Technology & Product to ensure all 3P solutions align with technical requirements and architectural standards.
• Work closely with Revenue Operations to measure and report on the sales productivity impact of all tooling investments.

Vendor & Lifecycle Management:

• Act as the main point of contact for 3P sales tooling partners, holding vendors accountable to roadmaps that resolve existing challenges and implement enhancements.
• Serve as the central DRI for tooling licensing, access management, and permissioning to accelerate decision-making and reduce operational friction.

Execution & Enablement:

• Partner with Enablement to drive adoption and best practices for 3P tools across sales teams, and track adoption and sentiment.
• Develop a centralized repository for tooling documentation and best practices to resolve current information silos.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will be driving…

• Tooling Optimization: Drive the evaluate, renew, and retire decisions that move us toward fewer, better tools and a 1P-first stack where possible.
• Governance in Motion: Optimize and oversee tooling governance council cycles and decision calendar running, ensuring fiscal discipline and eliminating redundant "shadow" procurement.
• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with GTM Technology, Product, Sales Leadership, Revenue Operations, and the Sales Analytics AI pod to align technical requirements with business goals and productivity outcomes.
• Tooling Optimization and ROI: Analyze usage data and performance metrics to derive actionable insights, identifying trends and providing recommendations to evolve or decommission tools to maximize ROI.
• Sales Productivity Strategy: Collaborate with Sales leads across all lines of business to identify friction points and implement 3P or AI-enabled solutions that accelerate the sales cycle and improve rep efficiency.
• Vendor Roadmap Influence: Be the key point of contact for your 3P vendors, providing structured feedback and holding them accountable to committed roadmaps and SLAs.

We’re excited about you because you have…

• A bachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Engineering, or a related field.
• Experience in Sales Operations, GTM Technology, or Sales Strategy, ideally in a fast-paced tech or e-commerce environment.
• Experience managing SaaS tools and vendor relationships, with exposure to renewals and contracts in partnership with Procurement and Legal.
• Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to distill technical tooling challenges into clear business cases for leadership and the tooling governance council.
• The ability to navigate large datasets to measure tooling adoption and business impact.
• Demonstrated experience in driving operational rigor and governance in a decentralized environment.
• An Architect at Heart – You think in systems, not just features; you treat every broken process as a build opportunity and every data gap as a use case waiting to be deployed.
• Entrepreneurial – You have a bias toward action, an ownership mentality, and the ability to thrive in a constantly changing environment.
• Gritty – You are willing to roll up your sleeves to map complex workflows, diagnose gaps, and do whatever it takes to make our tooling stack successful.
• A Relationship-Builder – You can influence and motivate stakeholders at all levels, from technical engineers to frontline sales managers.
• Operational & Rigorous – You independently translate high-level strategy into actionable project plans with strict attention to detail and efficiency.

Qualifications

• Experience: 6+ years in Sales Operations, GTM systems and tooling, or Sales Strategy, ideally supporting a sales tech stack; tech or marketplace experience preferred.
• Strategic Execution: Demonstrated success in leading cross-functional initiatives, hitting goals, and succeeding in a complex, fast-moving environment.
• Analytical Prowess: Excellent analytical thinker who can deliver actionable recommendations from complex usage and productivity datasets; Salesforce and Excel experience required, SQL preferred.
• AI-Native Builder: Proven explorer of AI tooling to drive efficiency; experience mapping complex operational workflows and architecting AI-enabled solutions. You are comfortable using tools like Claude or ChatGPT to prototype automation that eliminates manual work and accelerates decision-making.
• Communication: Expert communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to manage multiple vendors and internal stakeholders simultaneously.
• Systems Thinking: Experience with the end-to-end lifecycle of sales tools—from process discovery and technical requirement gathering through to prototype, deployment, and global enablement.

Nice to Haves

• Experience with the "Modern Sales Stack"
• Experience in procurement or managing large-scale SaaS budgets.
• Background in process improvement methodologies (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma) or project management certifications.

If you are a seasoned leader with a passion for optimizing technology to drive business results and want to be part of a dynamic, growing organization, we encourage you to apply for the Manager, Sales Strategy & Operations (Sales Tooling) position at DoorDash.

About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

You will develop and evolve the tooling ecosystem that hardware engineers rely on every day — from hardware compilers and IR transformations to simulation, debugging, and automation infrastructure. The work spans software engineering, compiler concepts, and practical hardware workflows, with direct impact on how quickly and effectively we design next-generation AI systems.

You’ll collaborate closely with architects, RTL designers, and verification engineers to translate real engineering friction into durable, scalable tooling solutions.

In this role you will:

- Build and improve the software tooling that makes hardware teams faster: compilation, IR transforms, RTL generation, simulation, debug, and automation.

- Extend and integrate hardware compiler stacks (frontends, IR passes, lowering, scheduling, codegen to Verilog/SystemVerilog) and connect them to real design workflows.

- Improve developer experience and reliability: reproducible builds, better error messages, faster iteration loops, and dependable CI and regression infrastructure.

- Work closely with designers and verification engineers to turn real pain points into durable tools.

- Dive into RTL when needed: read and reason about Verilog/SystemVerilog to debug issues, validate tool output, and improve debuggability.

- Be willing to go all the way down the stack when necessary, including gate-level views, synthesis results, and implementation artifacts.

- Help enable PPA optimization loops by building analysis and automation around area, timing, and power tradeoffs, and by improving tooling that impacts those outcomes.

You might thrive in this role if:

- Demonstrated ability to build and maintain software (projects, internships, research, open source, or equivalent experience).

- Strong CS fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, debugging, and software design.

- Proficiency in at least one of Rust, C++, or Python (and willingness to learn the rest).

- Familiarity with digital design concepts and the ability to read RTL (Verilog/SystemVerilog) or equivalent hardware descriptions.

- Familiarity with compiler or IR-based ideas (representations, passes, transformations, lowering), through coursework or projects.

- Comfort operating in ambiguity and iterating quickly with users of your tools.

Nice to have skills:

- Exposure to compiler and hardware toolchains such as XLS/DSLX, LLVM, Chisel/FIRRTL, CIRCT/MLIR, other novel hardware languages (e.g. HardCaml, SpinalHDL, Spade, PyMTL, Clash, BlueSpec, PyRope)

- Experience with Verilog tooling ecosystems (Yosys/RTLIL, Verilator, Slang) or writing tooling around them.

- Experience with build and test infrastructure (Bazel, CI systems, fuzzing, performance testing).

- Prior work touching synthesis, place and route, static timing analysis, or other PPA-related workflows.
